summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list.

findings.title: Search query injected as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading puts the q URL parameter into the page as unescaped HTML. Nothing sanitizes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect refetches on every render
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency list, so it runs after every render. Each run sets a new results array, which triggers another render.
findings.consequence: Every visit to the search page sends requests to the products API in an endless loop. This wastes client and server resources.
findings.fix: Pass [query] as the effect's dependency list.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: The component returns early when q is empty, before useState and useEffect run. The number of hook calls therefore changes between renders.
findings.consequence: React throws a hooks-order error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.problem: The change deletes the only search input form in the repository. The empty-query branch asks users to type a term but shows no input.
findings.consequence: Users who open the search page have no way to enter a query. Search is reachable only by editing the URL.
findings.fix: Keep the form with input name q on this page, or add one elsewhere.

findings.title: Search promise rejection unhandled
findings.problem: The searchProducts function throws when the response is not ok. The effect chains no catch, so the rejection is never handled.
findings.consequence: A failed search leaves stale or empty results with no error shown to the user. The browser only logs an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that records an error state and render a message for it.

findings.title: Search params read without a Suspense boundary
findings.problem: The page calls useSearchParams with no Suspense boundary around it. Next 15 requires one for prerendered pages.
findings.consequence: The production build can fail on the search route with a missing Suspense boundary error.
findings.fix: Move the client logic into a child component. Render that component inside Suspense from the page.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.problem: Each li in the results map has no key prop. Product has a stable id field available.
findings.consequence: React logs a missing key warning on every render. React also cannot reuse elements correctly when results change.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches and renders results and handles an empty query. The change adds no test for this behaviour.
findings.consequence: Regressions in query handling and result rendering will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a component test covering the empty query, a successful search and a failed search.
